Sparse presence-absence incidence from the native engine

Source: R/pam_incidence.R
pam_incidence.Rd

Streams an occurrence source through the tiled C++ engine and returns the incidence matrix itself — the PAM — instead of marginals: a n_units x n_species sparse object built from (unit, species) pairs accumulated in the shared bitset or the sort fallback. This is the scalable replacement for the dense get_geo_pam path, which is meant for small inputs.

Usage

pam_incidence(
  env_files,
  occ = NULL,
  occ_file = NULL,
  occ_polygons = NULL,
  poly_field = NULL,
  poly_layer = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  all_touched = TRUE,
  occ_dump = NULL,
  space = c("geo", "env"),
  format = c("dgCMatrix", "ij"),
  mins = NULL,
  maxs = NULL,
  nbs = c(30L, 30L),
  poly_chunk_rows = 256L,
  tile_rows = 512,
  threads = 1,
  max_bitset_mb = 1024,
  max_out_mb = 4096
)

Arguments

env_files

Raster paths (or a file-backed SpatRaster). For space = "geo" only the grid geometry is used; occ cells are terra cellnumbers on this grid. For space = "env" one multi-band file or D single-band files supply the environmental values.

occ, occ_file, occ_polygons, poly_field, poly_layer, species, all_touched, poly_chunk_rows

Identical to pam_env_engine.

occ_dump

Optional XPOC dump of the emitted pairs (polygon source only), reusable via occ_file.

space

"geo" (cells; default) or "env" (env bins).

format

"dgCMatrix" (default; a units x species Matrix::dgCMatrix of 1s, the canonical PAM object) or "ij" (a data.frame(i, j) of raw 1-based indices — i = unit id: terra cellnumber for space = "geo" or env-bin index for space = "env"; j = index into species). "dgCMatrix" requires the Matrix package (in Suggests).

mins, maxs, nbs

Binning range and bins per dimension; space = "env" only (same defaults as pam_env_engine).

tile_rows, threads, max_bitset_mb

Same as pam_env_engine.

max_out_mb

Feasibility cap (MB) for the returned incidence (nnz * 16 B as triplets). Default 4096 (~268 M pairs). Larger streams belong on disk via occ_dump.

Value

A list with pam (the sparse incidence object in the requested format), species, kernel ("bitmap"/"sort"), space, nnz, richness (species per unit), footprint (units per species), ncols, nrows, n_skipped and n_out_of_range.

Details

Two incidence spaces are supported. space = "geo" uses raster cells as units (the streaming geographic PAM: each row is a raster cell, i.e. a terra cellnumber); env_files then supplies only the grid template — its values are never read. With space = "env" units are the D-dimensional environmental bins over env_files, exactly as in pam_env_engine.

Scale behaviour is explicit rather than silent: the triplets must fit max_out_mb (nnz * 16 B) to be marshalled to R, the geo co-occurrence accumulator cannot export incidence (it never retains the pairs), and at sweep scale (22.5e9 pairs) the honest output is the on-disk XPOC written by occ_dump, not an R object — an informative error is thrown otherwise.

See also

pam_env_engine (marginals without the matrix), pam_jaccard (similarity from the same incidence), get_geo_pam (dense small-input path), has_gdal

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
if (has_gdal()) {
  # Streaming geographic PAM straight from polygons:
  pam_incidence("template.tif", occ_polygons = "ranges.gpkg",
                poly_field = "sciname")
}
} # }
